summary: Ferdinand Christian Baur worked in religious studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen and Evangelisches Stift Tübingen (~1809–1814), and later held a post at the University of Tübingen from ~1826 to 1860.

Ferdinand Hitzig was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. After studying under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and completing his Habilitation at Marburg, he served at Marburg as associate professor, full professor, and Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin, he taught at Deutsch-Chinesische Hochschule, Peking University, China Medical University, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, Humboldt University, and UC Berkeley.

Ferdinand Sommer was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Rudolf Thurneysen at Freiburg. He completed his Habilitation at Leipzig and held professorships at Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Geneva, Berlin, Paris, and Leipzig, earning his PhD in Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and others. He taught at the EPHE and served as professor at Geneva (1891–1913).
Ferdinand von Eckstein worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer (~1808–1812) and was a member of the Société Asiatique.

Ferenc Ruzsa specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fazekas Mihály Gimnázium (~1971–1975) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982), where he held a post as kari munkatárs starting around 1982.
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nalanda University and completed doctoral research supervised by Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at the National University of San Marcos (~1932–1940), he taught at the University of Buenos Aires and directed the Center of Buddhist Studies (~1990–2017).
Filipp Fortunatov studied under Georg Curtius (~1871–1872) and Michel Bréal (~1872–1873).
Filippo Marsili works in Sinology and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and held a post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

Finnian M. M. Gerety is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at Harvard in 2015, held a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018), and was a visiting assistant professor at Brown University (attested 2020).
Fiona Ross works in Indology and other fields. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1980–1988) and held posts at Tiro Typeworks and the University of Reading (~2003).

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist educated at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Sanskrit College and University before holding a chair at King's College London and serving as librarian at the India Office.

Flavio Geisshuesler specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Bern, Lausanne, and Virginia (PhD under David Germano ~2013–2019), and held posts at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Sydney.
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bucharest, Waseda, Peking University, and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen), and held posts at Kansai Medical University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Florinda De Simini works in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2016) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2019).

Fok Tou-hui was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies, and Otani University, and taught at CUHK from ~1972 to 1999.
